system.summary: Simple substitution of German in numbers 2-96, one number per letter (90 and 96 both s; 26 = u/v; 15 = i/j), numbers separated by colons and words by a cross; a nomenclator of capital, Greek and doubled letters (Λ Eure Excellenz, Φ Königliche Majestät, Σ Kaiserliche Majestät, XX alliance, ZZ defensiv, YY offensiv, X Kurz, W Bremen, m Pommern ...), sometimes with figures as suffix. The same key enciphers French in the Prague letter of October 1657.
system.notes: 90 occurs only once in the original letters; 96 is the usual s. Letters are often written twice (original and copy) in the volume. Distinct symbols counted in the originals: 30 numbers and 75 nomenclator symbol forms as transcribed (some forms are variants of one symbol).

prior_solution.where: In the volume: decipherments of the time (img 112-113 for img 110/109; img 157 right-158 left for L18; img 169 right for L25), interlinear decipherments over img 132, 136, 138, 140 and 171, and 19th-century notes in Danish (img 124-125, 137, 138, probably by E. Gigas). In print: summaries in Danish only, E. Gigas, Grev Bernardino de Rebolledo (1883), pp. 282-297, and J. A. Fridericia, Adelsvældens sidste Dage (1894), pp. 238-245 and n. 62, who thanks Gigas for a private decipherment of Sehested's letters, never printed; one German phrase is quoted ("die Gemüther alhie nicht wenig ermunteret"). DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry: no entry (11 Nov 2026). The German text of the cipher passages is not in print as far as we found.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target and set the rules (protocol and held-out lines hashed before the measurement; one measurement). Claude Opus 5.5 agents recorded the key on the interlinear decipherment of img 132, checked it on the clear of img 112, transcribed the 27 letters in seven batches, decoded, read and wrote up. No human checked the transcription or the reading.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout (key relevé, measurement, transcription, reading, write-up)

solution.what: Letter values recorded word by word on the interlinear decipherment of the time over img 132; checked on img 110 against the clear of the time img 112 (30 words, word for word).
One pre-registered measurement on held-out lines (img 145 left, 318 numbers): letter score -2.023 vs best of 900 controls -3.693; word-list share 0.569 vs 0.078; 1 number outside the key.
27 letters (and 5 cipher copies) transcribed number by number by seven agents, about 43,000 numbers.
Decoded mechanically and read by sense: 6013 cipher words, 5903 certain, 90 probable, 19 restored, 1 unresolved; copies agree with originals at 76-98% of words.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Letter values taken from the interlinear decipherment of the time on img 132 and confirmed on the clear of the time img 112; nomenclator values from glosses and clears of the time, the rest by the sense.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.md, cipher words of the 27 original letters (nomenclator symbols not counted): 5903 certain + 90 probable = 5993 of 6013 = 99.7%; 19 restored and 1 unresolved word not counted. Counted by the contributor's script (fiche.py).

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (protocol SHA-256 525288c0...; held-out transcription SHA-256 e2b4b59e...). Reservation: the agent knew the key while transcribing the held-out lines.

credits.note: transcription of 27 letters, key checked and completed, held-out measurement, reading (99.7%) and summaries: Brice Dudout with Claude Opus 5.5 agents

texts.label: L01, to the chancellor, Vienna 17/27 Jan. 1657 (with P.S.)
texts.summary: Sehested refers to his letter to the king; Kurz, at first surprised that no one came with full powers, took the matter up seriously on 14/24 Jan after conferring with La Fuente and gave the enclosed answer; Sehested asks the chancellor for the promised papers. P.S.: a breach between the Emperor and France is expected; forced levies; the French army put at 50,000; Rákóczi already in Poland, for himself rather than for Sweden; rumour of a Saxon marriage for the young king; Kurz flatters Sehested and has attached Windischgrätz to him to sound him out.

reading_review.by: Claude Opus 5.5 agent of Brice Dudout (one reader)
reading_review.note: Decoded text read letter by letter as German sentences; the words outside the period word list were checked one by one; five letters are confirmed by a second cipher copy and two by a clear of the time. Grade B: no human reader, transcription by AI agents only, and some 20 nomenclator symbols rest on the sense or are open.

texts.label: L02, to the king, Vienna 17/27 Jan. 1657
texts.summary: To the king: Sehested greeted Kurz on the alliance and the 'secret'; Kurz took it ad referendum, then reported that the Emperor is not averse to the defensive alliance proposed by the king but expects the draft and conditions from Denmark; the 'secret' once mentioned to Castel Rodrigo no longer matters. On 14/24 Jan Kurz asked for haste and for the inclusion of the States General.

texts.label: L03, to the king, Vienna 7/17 Feb. 1657 (date read 28/7; Gigas: 17 Feb.)
texts.summary: To the king: nothing new; spirits in Vienna raised by Rebolledo's favourable report on Danish armaments, passed to the Emperor by La Fuente on 2/12 Feb; passage through Friuli refused to the Turk; the Swiss rejected France's threefold proposal (Alsace); birth of an archduke on 1/11 Feb; Rákóczi advancing in Poland, Danzig seeking neutrality.

texts.label: L04, to the chancellor, Vienna 7/17 Feb. 1657 (with P.S.)
texts.summary: To the chancellor: the ministers await the resolution and full powers; ciphering has worn out his eyes, so no duplicates; news as in the letter to the king; his reports to Kurz confirmed by Rebolledo. P.S.: talks in Paris with the cardinal; a Franco-Swedish offensive and defensive alliance is believed concluded.

texts.label: L05, to the king, Vienna 14/24 Feb. 1657
texts.summary: To the king: the Emperor has consented orally to the cession of Bremen; should Sehested press for a written promise, and claim Bremen as a see or as a secularised duchy (better: hereditary)? The Turkish danger is played up; new patents for 7,000 men; an envoy is sent to [H].

texts.label: L06, to the chancellor, Vienna 14/24 Feb. 1657 (glossed original; two cipher copies)
texts.summary: To the chancellor: Kurz would discuss Bremen only after the alliance; Sehested argues that Danish preparations are ready and that general peace is impossible while Sweden holds Pomerania, Mecklenburg and Bremen. On 11/21 Feb the Emperor, Kurz and La Fuente conferred: the king will be satisfied; the Danish minister at The Hague should block ratification of the Swedish-Dutch treaty and bring the States General into the alliance. Kurz then announced the Emperor's consent to the transfer of Bremen. P.S. at nine o'clock: the Emperor resolves on an offensive alliance and awaits the full powers urgently.

texts.label: L07, proposition to Emperor Ferdinand III (audience of 18/28 Feb. 1657), copy
texts.summary: Proposition to Emperor Ferdinand III (audience of 18/28 Feb): Swedish possession of the duchies of Pomerania and Bremen endangers the Empire and Denmark and threatens the peace of Westphalia; if the king must carry his arms against Bremen, he hopes the Emperor will not oppose it and will support it with a diversion in Pomerania; he will wait for the Emperor's resolution and asks his advice and how far he may count on his help.

P.S.: inclusion of the States General pressed; La Fuente wavers.

texts.label: L10, to the chancellor, Vienna 4/14 Mar. 1657
texts.summary: To the chancellor: the Emperor has resolved to conclude the offensive and defensive alliance quickly; Bremen better in Danish hands; send the full powers at once. Colonel Garnier secretly seeks help for Poland against Rákóczi; a secret imperial envoy urges Rákóczi to withdraw; the Emperor will act this summer, where is not yet known.

texts.label: L11, to the chancellor, Vienna 7/17 Mar. 1657
texts.summary: To the chancellor: Kurz says the Emperor now wants a general offensive and defensive alliance binding both sides; Sehested took it ad referendum. The States General should come later as an accessory. Questions: should Denmark insist on 'Königliche Majestät' instead of 'Königliche Würden', on a recredential, and on a written promise for Bremen?
